solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film Abel

definitions.meaning: a 1949 Carol Reed thriller set in post-war Vienna, starring Orson Welles
after Adam and his first son Cain, Abel was the next male human in Genesis, hence the third

explanation.surface: A bare label, as if naming a film called Abel.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis gives Adam, then Cain, then Abel, so Abel is literally the third male to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: the title of the classic Graham Greene film, and a biblical description of Abel.

clue.text: Highly explosive marine island

parts.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive
RM stands for Royal Marines, so a marine is an RM

explanation.surface: A dangerous explosive device found on a sea island.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands, near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Herm is a small Channel Island, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Article lady's bringing up for Greek hero

parts.note: the definite article is the word 'the'

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Sue's: a woman's name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in which a woman raises the subject of a Greek hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing up' suits a down clue, where the letters are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus, slayer of the Minotaur, is a celebrated figure of Greek legend, so an example of a hero.

clue.text: Car racing in outskirts of Dewsbury

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so take the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A motor race held on the edge of the Yorkshire town of Dewsbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Dewsbury is a town in West Yorkshire; its outer letters are D and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Indy is short for IndyCar, the American form of open-wheel motor racing based on the Indianapolis 500.

clue.text: Report group of ten from ecclesiastical district

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is said aloud rather than written

parts.note: denary means based on or relating to ten, as in the denary system

explanation.surface: A church diocese issuing a report from a committee of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: DENARY strictly means relating to tens; spoken, it sounds close to the church word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deanery is a group of parishes under a rural dean, a division of a diocese.

clue.text: Bath water

definitions.meaning: the English city of Bath was in the former county of ... and lies on the river of that name
a river is a body of water, and the Celtic word ... itself means river

explanation.surface: Simply the water in a bath tub.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a city in south-west England; capitalised at the start, it hides its proper-noun sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Avon runs through the city of Bath, which was in the county named after it.

clue.text: Cha at the slightest opportunity

parts.note: these three letters are the first half of the word chance, so the answer read as wordplay describes them

explanation.surface: Grabbing a cup of tea whenever the moment allows.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is British slang for tea, which sets up the tea-break picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a small or slight possibility, as in 'given half a chance'.

clue.text: Plant from garden gone awry right to be included

indicators.note: the single letter is put inside the scrambled letters
awry means askew or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant that has turned out badly in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' sits at the front and is the definition; 'awry' and 'to be included' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The green dragon is a woodland herb, Arisaema dracontium, a relative of the cuckoo pint.

clue.text: Whitish rubber substance, something that is balanced on furrow first, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be spoken and heard, not spelt

parts.words: something that is balanced on furrow first
parts.note: a furrow is a gutter, and something balanced on a perch is a percher; with furrow first this gives gutter percher

explanation.surface: A rubbery material described as something balanced on a groove.
explanation.walkthrough: GUTTER PERCHER, spoken in a non-rhotic British accent, sounds like the name of the latex.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutta-percha is a natural latex from Malaysian trees, once used to insulate cables and make golf balls.

clue.text: Tribesman with Edward shortly travelling round dry part of Africa

indicators.note: travelling round suggests letters moving about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A tribesman and a friend called Ed making a journey across arid Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling round' is the anagram signal; 'Tribesman' is fodder, not a synonym to look up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Namib is a coastal desert in south-west Africa, among the driest places on Earth.

clue.text: Commemorating having binge with claret flowing

indicators.note: flowing implies movement, so the letters are poured into a new order

explanation.surface: Marking an occasion with a drinking spree as red wine pours freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' rearranges BINGE and CLARET together.
explanation.definitionFit: To celebrate an anniversary is to commemorate it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: One suspicious bloomer

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
rum is British slang for odd or suspicious

explanation.surface: Someone suspicious who keeps making blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' seems to mean a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a flowering plant, so in crossword terms it is a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Unsophisticated individual leaving worship centre

indicators.note: leaving says the letter departs from the longer word

parts.note: naive means innocent or unsophisticated
I, the letter for one, stands for a single individual

explanation.surface: A simple soul walking out of church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I out of NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The nave is the central body of a church, where the congregation sits for services.

clue.text: Prophetic lot developing influenza shortly

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate

indicators.note: developing suggests change, so the short word's letters are reordered

parts.note: flu is the shortened form of influenza

explanation.surface: A grim prediction that many people will soon come down with flu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' works on a word the clue only defines: an indirect anagram, which many setters frown on.
explanation.definitionFit: Fateful can mean ominous or portentous of what is to come, close to prophetic.

clue.text: Young lady from Scotland did not finish drink

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter is lost

parts.note: lassie is the Scots word for a girl

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl leaving her drink half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did not finish' drops the last letter E of LASSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lassi is a yoghurt-based beverage from India, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Short biographical sketch favouring female going to isolated area in France

parts.note: pro means in favour of
île is French for island, an area cut off by water

explanation.surface: A brief life story of a woman who heads for a remote corner of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a short article outlining a person's life and character.

clue.text: Play quietly before dramatist gives expression of contempt

parts.note: the musical instruction to play quietly is piano, written P
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken performance before a playwright, who scoffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play quietly' is a single direction: the musical marking p, for piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an old-fashioned exclamation of disdain or impatience.

clue.text: Impertinent Neddy entering Seychelles

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
a neddy is a donkey, an ass

explanation.surface: A cheeky donkey arriving in the Seychelles.
explanation.walkthrough: Neddy is a British pet name for a donkey; 'entering' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy means cheeky or saucy, a synonym of impertinent.

clue.text: Round detonator first used by head of a branch of the Mafia

definitions.text: head of a branch of the Mafia

indicators.note: first places the detonator word before the round one

parts.note: a cap is a small explosive charge that sets off a larger one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A mob boss being the first to use a detonator in a round of attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts CAP ahead of O, the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A capo is the boss of a crime family or of one of its crews, from the Italian for head.

clue.text: Actors in this came back for a month

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RADA, the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London, trains actors

explanation.surface: Performers returning to a place after a month away.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's leading drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is the twelfth month of the Jewish religious calendar, around February and March.

clue.text: Skater loses time going round glacial ridge

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters turn and spin into a new order
losing means a letter is taken away

explanation.surface: An ice skater on a glacier, short of time as they circle a ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes T out of SKATER to leave SKAER, which 'going round' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An eskar, or esker, is a long winding ridge of gravel left by a glacier's meltwater.

clue.text: Was relating to the ear, one of the foreign articles

parts.note: ex means former, what was once so
otic is the adjective for the ear
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A clumsy statement about a foreign object that was linked to hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are unusual items from distant lands, so exotic goods or objects.

clue.text: Strike a second match?

parts.note: seems to call for a second match struck, but means setting fire once more to something that has gone out

explanation.surface: A sports fan calling for a replay or a second strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sporting fixture and 'strike' a walkout, but both belong to lighting a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something again is to set fire to it a second time, much as striking another match does.

clue.text: Flying cab?

parts.note: a taxi driven at speed is flying along, but here the cab genuinely flies

explanation.surface: A taxi rushing through the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' looks like speeding, but it is literal: the vehicle is airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: An air taxi is a small aircraft hired for short trips, an airborne equivalent of a hired car.

clue.text: Cavity with receiver firmly fixed

parts.note: a well is a deep shaft or hole in the ground
a set is a radio or television receiver

explanation.surface: A telephone receiver lodged securely in a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-set describes something solidly placed or firmly established.

clue.text: Charlie gives expression of triumphant surprise finding salmon

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
oho is an exclamation of gleeful discovery

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie crowing in delight on landing a salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: The coho is a species of Pacific fish, also called silver salmon.

clue.text: Call off moving energetically, drive out

indicators.note: off says the letter is dropped from the word it goes with

parts.note: to roust is to stir or rouse, to move vigorously
a call is a ring on the phone, and R can stand for ring

explanation.surface: Cancelling a hurried move and driving someone away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call off' reads as cancel, but 'Call' gives R and 'off' drops it. Using R for a ring, a phone call, is a stretch; even the puzzle's blogger was unsure of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to expel or force them from a place or position.

clue.text: Second record on computer

parts.note: B is second in rank, as in a B grade or B-team
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Keeping a duplicate record on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, since a blog is a web log, a computer-hosted record.
explanation.definitionFit: Blog shortens web log, an online diary or journal kept on the internet.

clue.text: Australian managed islands

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: An Australian who once ran some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aran Islands are a group of three in Galway Bay, an example of islands.

clue.text: Some Australasian, but not from here

definitions.text: Some Australasian, but not from here

indicators.note: some of a word means part of it, so a run of its letters is taken

explanation.surface: Someone from Australasia insisting they are not from this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits within the word Australasian, yet someone from Australasia is not from the continent named, so the clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent is the region lying north of Australasia, part of the name but a different place.

clue.text: Hearing he's a scientist

parts.note: seems to report news of someone's profession, but describes a specialist who studies the ear and hearing

explanation.surface: Learning by word of mouth that someone works in science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like 'being told', but it is the subject of the scientist's study.
explanation.definitionFit: This specialist studies hearing and its disorders, testing ears and fitting aids.

clue.text: Immediately using normal system

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a ... is a conventional, orthodox approach

explanation.surface: Switching at once to the standard method.
explanation.definitionFit: Straightway is an old word for at once; split, it also suggests doing things the straight, conventional way.
